"Create a fully playable 3D voxel sandbox game titled exactly MemeticBox. This must be an extreme physics-driven gore sandbox that closely recreates the real MemeticBox experience. Use a hybrid first-person and third-person camera. Prioritize heavy, messy, satisfying destruction.
Voxel Style @COMMENT_BODY@ Character Models
Pure 3D voxel art with high detail.
Every human character is built from thousands of voxels with full multi-layer anatomy:
Clothing layer (fabric that tears and flies off)
Skin layer
Muscle and fat layer
Bone layer
Internal organs (heart, lungs, brain, intestines, liver, stomach)
Individual eyes with pupils that can be destroyed
Detailed faces, varied hairstyles, different clothing styles, skin tones, and body types.
Player hands and weapons must also be high-quality voxels.
Extreme Gore, Dismemberment @COMMENT_BODY@ Gibs
Full layered destruction: bullets and blades cut through clothing → skin → muscle → bone → organs.
Complete dismemberment: heads, arms, legs, and torsos can separate and become independent physics objects.
Advanced gib system: heavily damaged bodies explode into many flying gibs (flesh chunks, muscle, bone fragments, organs, clothing pieces, blood voxels).
Gibs fly with realistic force and direction, bounce, roll, leave blood trails, and stay on the map.
Weapon-specific gib behavior:
Rifles/pistols = penetrating holes and focused damage
Explosives = wide spray of many gibs
Katana/blades = clean slices and large separated limbs
Flamethrower = burnt, charred, crumbling gibs
Volumetric blood: arterial spray, red mist, pooling, staining ground and clothes, long-lasting blood voxels.
Red popup text: “CASUALTY REPORT – CIVILIAN KILLED” whenever a civilian dies.
Ragdoll, Stagger @COMMENT_BODY@ Balance
Characters stagger and flinch from light/medium hits instead of instantly ragdolling.
Stagger causes slowed movement and temporary imbalance while staying on their feet.
Heavy hits, headshots, or repeated damage cause full ragdoll.
Ragdolls feel heavy with proper momentum, tumbling, joint limits, and bouncing.
Losing a limb causes strong stagger or collapse of the remaining body.
Lightly wounded characters can slowly try to stand back up after a few seconds.
Weapons @COMMENT_BODY@ Controls
Bottom weapon bar with numbered buttons:
Guard (fists)
Rifle
Deagle
Grenade
Flame (flamethrower)
Kat (katana)
More… (shotgun, sniper, chainsaw, knife, etc.)
Working LASER button that toggles a clear red laser sight beam on the current weapon, with a red dot on surfaces and enemies.
FIRE button, RELOAD button, JUMP button, on-screen joystick.
Unique sounds, muzzle flashes, and impact effects for every weapon.
Visible reloading with magazines.
God Tools
Purple “GOD TOOLS” button opens:
Grab @COMMENT_BODY@ Throw
Stretch limbs until they tear
Lightning
Impale / spike
Hang
Force push/pull
Spawn explosion
Spawn fire
Freeze time / slow motion
Laser Eyes (fire burning red laser beams from the eyes that damage and ignite targets)
Photo mode / free camera
Clean all bodies
Spawn civilian / enemy / vehicle
Maps @COMMENT_BODY@ World
Start in a large open grassy field with dirt paths, trees, a green military jeep, and several walking civilians.
Additional switchable maps:
Small town with destructible buildings
Hospital / close-quarters
Dark forest
Arena
All maps are fully voxel-destructible. Blood and gibs persist.
NPCs
Civilians walk around, react to gunfire, scream, run, and can be killed.
Varied detailed appearances.
Clear hit reactions and voice responses.
Sounds
Realistic gunshots, reloads, explosions, flamethrower, blade swings
Heavy body and gib impact sounds
Pain screams, death sounds, civilian panic
Laser on/off sound
Satisfying squelch and thud on impacts
UI
Top bar: SANDBOX mode, HP bar, STA bar, counter, 1P, CLEAN button
Bottom weapon selection bar
Clear God Tools button
Smooth controls and strong hit feedback
Possible camera blood splatter on close kills
Make every system work together: layered anatomy, extreme gibs, realistic stagger-to-ragdoll, working laser sight, laser eyes, detailed models, and heavy physics. Start the player in the grassy field with a rifle equipped and civilians nearby so everything can be tested immediately.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable MemeticBox voxel sandbox game with physics-driven combat, gore effects, God Tools, NPCs, and multiple maps.

## Requirements
- Pure 3D voxel style with detailed, destructible characters and weapons.
- Extreme dismemberment/gib effects, blood, stagger-to-ragdoll, and persistent debris.
- Hybrid first-person/third-person camera.
- Working weapons, laser sight, mobile controls, map switching, UI, and God Tools.
- Start with rifle equipped in a grassy field beside walking civilians.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a self-contained Three.js browser game in `index.html`.
- Used simplified voxel anatomy and stylized gore rather than fully realistic layered models.
- Added four switchable maps and a sandbox-style damage system.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the complete initial `index.html` implementation.
- Added grassy field, trees, dirt paths, jeep, houses, and multiple maps.
- Added voxel civilians with varied clothing and skin tones.
- Added weapon selection, firing, reloads, laser sight, grenade, flamethrower, katana, and guard options.
- Added stagger, death, shattered/physics debris, blood/gib-like particles, explosions, and map tools.
- Added God Tools panel with grab, push, lightning, blast, fire, slow time, spawn, clean, map change, and laser eyes.
- Added desktop and touch controls, HP/STA UI, weapon bar, camera toggle, and jump.
- Verified JavaScript syntax and opened the game in Chromium.
- Captured `screenshots/memeticbox.jpg`.

### Active
- None.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Improve gore fidelity with true layered anatomy, individual organ meshes, limb separation, and persistent blood pools.
2. Replace simplified target movement with a proper ragdoll and joint physics system.
3. Add weapon-specific audio, reload animations, muzzle flashes, and civilian panic/voice responses.
4. Inspect the browser screenshot and polish the visual presentation.

## Relevant Files
- `[index.html]`: Main and only implementation file for the complete game.
- `[screenshots/memeticbox.jpg]`: Latest viewport screenshot from browser verification.

## Important Context
- The development server was started on `http://localhost:3002`.
- Browser verification succeeded: the page rendered, the entry screen loaded, and `MemeticBox` was entered.
- The only browser console 404 was for `/favicon.ico`.
- Screenshot rendering used the preinstalled Chromium/SwiftShader environment.
